correctness.rationale: For a pair of nonadjacent vertices, each sees S-a-b one-neighbors; for an unmatched universal vertex, each sees S-x. Splitting even and odd total vertex counts yields complete threshold tables. Even total count has a balanced invariant involution; odd total count has only two critical levels, and every periodic nonuniform point has uniform pair-types and universal bits, permitting an exact two-cycle classification. The orbit formulas follow by labelled binomial choices, with division by two only where both phases belong to the same class. The proof bounds first periodic entry by one update for even u and three for odd u. Standalone labelled enumeration checks 261804 configurations in 44 families and two independent weighted-profile checks cover 288 families. Infinite quantifiers are justified by the symbolic case split, not by extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The inspected published general period-two theorem does not supply exact counts or sharp settling bounds. The primary 2014 full-text statements address random/unimodular graphs, and the 2022 orbit-enumeration results are restricted to trees. Searches of published mathematical records found a complete-multipartite parity automaton using XOR, not majority, and a static majority C-colouring result; neither implies a nonlinear majority orbit census. Earlier compared mathematical statements involve crown, prism, and Möbius-ladder graphs, not a dense complete graph with a deleted matching. Search nonhits do not establish priority, and the 1980 complete paper was inaccessible; risk is disclosed.

value.rationale: The count is a natural exact invariant of deterministic opinion dynamics on the complete multipartite family with part sizes at most two, interpolating between cocktail-party graphs and near-complete cliques. It yields a sharp parity-and-size existence classification: when u is odd and at least three, two-cycles vanish for one parity class, reappear in another, and disappear beyond an exact structural imbalance threshold. For even u the whole balanced binomial layer is periodic, while odd u can leave just two fixed points. These dramatic differences and a uniform three-update convergence law supply mathematical structure beyond a single computation or an unmotivated parameter slice. The counts are not implied by the generic period-two theorem; no downstream theorem is claimed.
